fact: INTIC presented the proposed National AI Strategy (ENIA) to the Mozambican AI Association; the report says it is still being developed through an ongoing multi-sector consultation (date given is the publication date, 2026-08-25, as the meeting date is not stated).

INTIC presented key elements of the proposed National AI Strategy to Vodacom Mozambique on 12 August 2026; the strategy is said to be undergoing consultation, public hearings and sectoral harmonisation, led by the Ministry of Communications and Digital Transformation through INTIC with UNESCO support.

At a 12 August 2026 meeting INTIC presented key elements of the proposed National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence to Vodacom Mozambique; the report describes it as still being developed within an ongoing consultation and sectoral harmonisation process.

INTIC presented the draft National AI Strategy at an ITU workshop in Kenya; INTIC says it is in its final drafting phase, with the technical part due by June 2026 before submission to the Council of Ministers (month is the publication month; no event date given).
The document is Draft 1 of the Estratégia Nacional de Inteligência Artificial (2026-2031), dated Maputo, April 2026, with eight pillars and INTIC reviewer comments marking it as a working draft.

Africa AI News reports INTIC presented a draft National AI Strategy at an ITU workshop in Kenya, with the technical component due by June 2026 before submission to the Council of Ministers; the draft (1 April 2026) was open to public consultation until 4 June 2026.

Africa AI News reports a National Commission for Artificial Intelligence was recently established by decree and will assess the final strategy before government submission, alongside a Multisectoral Working Group convened by the Minister of Communications and Digital Transformation; the document gives no exact date, so the publication month is used.
INTIC announced the first version of the proposed National AI Strategy was published on its portal for public consultation from 4 May to 4 June 2026, in Word and PDF versions.

AIM reports INTIC chairman Chemane said a National AI Strategy has been conceived, and the country is still seeking to establish a national strategy; the report does not say it was approved or launched.

INTIC's board chair said at the AI Impact Summit India in February 2026 that a proposal for a National AI Strategy was being drawn up with UNESCO support and ITU follow-up, and the article of 2026-05-15 still describes the strategy as being prepared.

Decree 14/2026 of 17 April 2026 creates the National AI Commission (CNIA) under the Council of Ministers, and gives its executive secretariat, the ICT regulatory authority, the task of coordinating implementation of the actions of the National AI Strategy.
